chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Supplicate for the provision while you are in the prescribed prayer and you are in prostration: O Best of those asked from, and O Best of the Givers! Grant me provision and grant my dependents from Your extensive bounty, for You are the Possessor of the Great Bounty.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication for seeking sustenance during prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) highlights the spiritual potency of supplicating during the humblest position of prayer, linking physical submission with divine generosity. It serves as a practical guide for believers to seek rizq not merely as material wealth, but as a manifestation of God's vast grace (fadl), reinforcing the Shia emphasis on the intercessory and responsive nature of the Imams' teachings.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Umar Al Yamani, from Zayd Al Shahaam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Supplicate for the sustenance during the Prescribed (Salāt) while you are in Sajdah, ‘O Best of the ones asked from, and O Best of the Givers! Grace me and Grace my dependants from Yourazwj Extensive Grace, for Youazwj are the One With the Magnificent Grace’’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Ibrahim ibn ‘Umar al-Yamani from Zayd al-Shahham from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “

When pleading for sustenance in the obligatory prayer during prostration say, ‘O the best to plead to, O the best provider, grant me and my family sustenance from Your vast munificence; You are the Great, the Generous.’”
